omissions.point: The Federal Reserve’s dual mandate is commonly framed as two objectives—maximum employment and stable prices—even though the statute also mentions moderate long-term interest rates.
omissions.evidence: The Fed’s mandate for monetary policy is commonly known as the dual mandate,” and explains that stable prices and broad job availability create conditions in which interest rates settle at moderate levels.

omissions.point: The 1978 Full Employment and Balanced Growth Act (Pub. L. 95-523, Oct. 27, 1978) did not create the objectives; it amended Section 2A (via §108) to change the reporting framework.
omissions.evidence: did **not** first create the objectives. Instead, it **amended Section 2A’s reporting framework**.
